title: Ten digests
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A tourist takes ten digests from the rack. All of them. The owner says one each. The tourist says they're free. The owner says one each is what free means. The tourist puts nine back. Wood, in the door, has never loved anyone more and would never say so.

panels.composition: The laundromat. A TOURIST in a sun hat with the whole slot of digests in her arms. The LAUNDRY owner at the counter.

balloons.text: One each is what free means.

image.prompt: a tourist in a sun hat holding an armful of small booklets taken from a wire rack while the laundromat owner watches from the counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Nine going back in the rack, one at a time, the tourist's face.

image.prompt: close on a tourist's hands returning booklets to a wire rack one at a time with a sour face, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD in the door with BARNABY. His face. The strip does not have a name for it.

image.prompt: a young man in a laundromat doorway with a small dog, his face showing something the strip has no name for, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner, back to folding. Not looking at Wood. Knowing.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner folding towels with her back turned, knowing she is being looked at, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'One each is what free means.' The face the strip has no name for.
